albums.blurb: Menahan Street Band is a Brooklyn instrumental soul collective led by guitarist and producer Thomas Brenneck, assembled from members of the Dap-Kings, the Budos Band, and Antibalas, and serving as the house band for Dunham Records, the Daptone subsidiary founded around them. This entirely instrumental debut was recorded in Brenneck's apartment studio on the Menahan Street that gave the band its name, and its horn-led, cinematic take on soul set the template for the backing work the group later did for Charles Bradley.
albums.reception: The title track was sampled by Jay-Z on “Roc Boys (And the Winner Is)…” from American Gangster, and the album's tracks have since been sampled by artists including 50 Cent, Kid Cudi, and Curren$y.

albums.blurb: The Chicago violinist and singer's third solo album, released on Righteous Babe Records in 2005, was the record where his mature style clicked into place: looped pizzicato violin, whistling, and wordplay-dense songwriting, after his earlier swing-revival work with Bowl of Fire. It contains “Fake Palindromes” and marked his commercial breakthrough, setting up the major-label follow-up Armchair Apocrypha.
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 85 out of 100, and Pitchfork later placed “Fake Palindromes” at number 331 on its list of the top 500 tracks of the 2000s.

albums.blurb: Melody's Echo Chamber is the project of French multi-instrumentalist Melody Prochet, and this debut was produced by Tame Impala's Kevin Parker, who ran her airy French- and English-language melodies through his saturated, tape-warped psych production. Released on Fat Possum and Weird World in 2012, it stood for six years as the project's only album until the follow-up Bon Voyage arrived in 2018.
albums.reception: The album received generally favorable reviews, with a Metacritic average of 79 based on 19 critics, including a 9/10 from Drowned in Sound and an 8/10 from Q.
